# im

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/pkg/im"
```

Package im provides read\-only structs, slices, and maps checked by immutago.

Choose the API for the data:

- Shared: read\-only fields; callers can store or return pointers.
- ByValue: keep read\-only value copies; use pointers through direct checked calls.
- Owner: publish a new ByValue object while readers finish with the previous one.
- FrozenSlice and FrozenMap: freeze a native collection without copying entries. Use Clone for an independent mutable copy.

Prepare a native collection in one local variable. After Freeze, use only the frozen value. Run immutago to enforce these rules; go build alone does not.

## func Unwrap

```go
func Unwrap[T any](value UncheckedValue[T]) *T
```

Unwrap returns the wrapped pointer, or nil for the zero UncheckedValue. Only the package that declares T can use Unwrap.

## type ByValue

ByValue marks a struct with read\-only fields. Values can be copied, stored, and returned. Pointers can stay local or pass to direct checked calls. They cannot be stored in fields or containers, saved globally, returned, or captured by closures. Use Owner to publish a new ByValue object for other code to read. Embed it by value. A named field or pointer embedding does not mark the struct. See https://github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/blob/main/docs/by-value.md for the complete forms.

```go
type ByValue struct{}
```

## type FrozenMap

FrozenMap is a read\-only map. Its zero value is empty. K and V must be immutable. Copies share the same read\-only entries.

```go
type FrozenMap[K comparable, V any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func FreezeMap

```go
func FreezeMap[K comparable, V any](values map[K]V) FrozenMap[K, V]
```

FreezeMap makes values read\-only without copying entries or allocating. Keep values in one local variable before Freeze. Afterward, read through the returned FrozenMap. The checker rejects aliases and use of the old map. Run immutago to enforce these rules; Freeze performs no runtime validation.

### func \(FrozenMap\[K, V\]\) All

```go
func (m FrozenMap[K, V]) All() iter.Seq2[K, V]
```

All returns an iterator over key\-value pairs in unspecified order. It reads frozen storage directly without making a copy. Each invocation starts a new map traversal and stops as soon as yield returns false.

### func \(FrozenMap\[K, V\]\) Clone

```go
func (m FrozenMap[K, V]) Clone() map[K]V
```

Clone returns an independent native map in O\(n\) time and space. It copies keys and values by value and preserves nil. Mutating the copy does not change the frozen map. Pointers still point to the same immutable objects; immutable types make deeper copying unnecessary.

### func \(FrozenMap\[K, V\]\) Get

```go
func (m FrozenMap[K, V]) Get(key K) (V, bool)
```

Get returns the value for key and whether it exists, using native map lookup. It allocates no storage and preserves Go's key equality rules.

### func \(FrozenMap\[K, V\]\) Len

```go
func (m FrozenMap[K, V]) Len() int
```

Len returns the number of entries in O\(1\) time without allocations.

## type FrozenSlice

FrozenSlice is a read\-only slice. Its zero value is empty. T must be immutable. Copies share the same read\-only entries.

```go
type FrozenSlice[T any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func FreezeSlice

```go
func FreezeSlice[T any](values []T) FrozenSlice[T]
```

FreezeSlice makes values read\-only without copying entries or allocating. Keep values in one local variable before Freeze. Afterward, read through the returned FrozenSlice. The checker rejects aliases and use of the old slice. Run immutago to enforce these rules; Freeze performs no runtime validation.

### func \(FrozenSlice\[T\]\) All

```go
func (s FrozenSlice[T]) All() iter.Seq2[int, T]
```

All returns an iterator over index\-value pairs in increasing index order. It reads frozen storage directly without making a copy. Each invocation starts at index zero and stops as soon as yield returns false.

### func \(FrozenSlice\[T\]\) At

```go
func (s FrozenSlice[T]) At(index int) T
```

At returns the element at index in O\(1\) time without allocations. It panics if index is out of range, as native slice indexing does.

### func \(FrozenSlice\[T\]\) Clone

```go
func (s FrozenSlice[T]) Clone() []T
```

Clone returns an independent native slice in O\(n\) time and space. It copies elements by value and preserves nil. Mutating the copy does not change the frozen slice. Pointers still point to the same immutable objects; immutable element types make deeper copying unnecessary.

### func \(FrozenSlice\[T\]\) Len

```go
func (s FrozenSlice[T]) Len() int
```

Len returns the number of elements in O\(1\) time without allocations.

## type Owner

Owner stores a replaceable pointer to a read\-only ByValue object. Load and Store are atomic; readers can continue to use an earlier object. The analyzer checks construction and pointer use. Declare a slot as a package variable or a direct named field of an unmarked struct. Its zero value is empty. An Owner value must not be copied. See https://github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/blob/main/docs/owner.md for the complete forms.

```go
type Owner[T any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func \(\*Owner\[T\]\) Load

```go
func (o *Owner[T]) Load() *T
```

Load returns the current pointer, or nil if the slot is empty. Keep the pointer local or pass it to a function that does not save it. It remains valid after a later Store. Go's garbage collector manages its lifetime.

### func \(\*Owner\[T\]\) Store

```go
func (o *Owner[T]) Store(value *T)
```

Store publishes a freshly constructed object.

## type Shared

Shared marks a struct with read\-only fields. Values and pointers to that struct can be copied, stored, and returned through the allowed source forms. Embed it by value. A named field or pointer embedding does not mark the struct. See https://github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/blob/main/docs/shared.md for the complete forms.

## type UncheckedValue

UncheckedValue holds a pointer to data whose immutability the analyzer does not prove. The package that declares T promises never to change the data after Trust.

UncheckedValue is an allowed stored type. Any package can store, copy, and pass it. Only the package that declares T can use Trust and Unwrap, so other packages reach the value only through the API of that package. See https://github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/blob/main/docs/unchecked-values.md for the complete forms.

```go
type UncheckedValue[T any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func Trust

```go
func Trust[T any](value *T) UncheckedValue[T]
```

Trust wraps value with an unchecked promise that it is immutable. It does not copy or freeze the data. Only the package that declares T can use Trust, and that package must not change the value after this call.
